name: Muslim American Society of Greater LA
mission: To nurture a balanced and living understanding of Islam for Muslims in America, raise up leaders equipped for sustained Islamic service, activate communities around prophetic principles and shared purpose, champion justice and equity in society, and engage non-Muslims with clarity and compassion about Islam as a God-centered way of life.
theoryOfChange: The Muslim American Society (MAS) of Greater LA utilizes a strategic framework that includes a Theory of Change and a 'Strategy House'. The 'Our Impact Areas' page on their website details five key impact areas: Islam to Muslims, Leadership Development, Community Mobilization, Social Justice, and Islam to Non-Muslims. For each impact area, the page outlines specific 'Subareas of Focus' and desired 'Outcomes', demonstrating a structured approach to achieving their goals. Furthermore, the organization introduced a 'Theory of Change framework' and a 'Strategy House' as a centerpiece of their transformation, which is described as a single page explaining their vision, mission, and six pillars, including 'Operate with Excellence'. It is also noted that 'Ninety-two percent of programs translated into Theory of Change templates' by the end of 2025. The organization also mentions 'Theory of Change retreats' as part of their Chapter Growth & Community Building initiatives.

strengths_deep_dive: The Muslim American Society of Greater LA demonstrates positive operational discipline through its core spending ratios. In FY2024, the organization recorded <cite id="3">$1,168,118 in revenue</cite> while directing <cite id="3">77.3% of expenses to functional programs</cite>. This surpasses the 75% baseline benchmark for nonprofit efficiency. Capital conversion is further optimized by minimal development overhead, requiring <cite id="1">only $0.03 in fundraising costs per dollar collected</cite>. With financial health supported by <cite id="1">3.6 months of operating reserves</cite>, the organization maintains an efficient platform for spiritual mentorship.
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in <cite id="4">1993</cite>, the Muslim American Society of Greater LA delivers religious mentorship and youth development initiatives across California. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="3">$1,168,118 in total revenue</cite> to expand its core community efforts. These initiatives include the <cite id="4">Tarbiya Mentorship Development Program</cite>, youth leadership workshops, and educational camps. The group operates with positive financial efficiency, maintaining a <cite id="3">79.4% program expense ratio</cite> in FY2024. This beats the standard 75% sector benchmark and leaves approximately one-fifth of spending for administrative needs. Fundraising remains exceptionally lean, as the charity spends <cite id="1">only $0.03 to raise every $1</cite>. The organization is <cite id="2">zakat-eligible under the fisabilillah category</cite>, providing a direct path for Muslim donors seeking targeted spiritual and leadership investments.
